We need to determine number of methyl (CH3) groups in the sample's molecule. We need the molecule structure. No SMILES given. We can retrieve NMR spectra? Probably need to infer from NMR data. But we have no data yet. We can request proton NMR spectra for a given SMILES, but we don't have SMILES. Maybe we can request carbon NMR spectra for sample at hand (unknown). The tool carbon_nmr_spectra returns spectra for sample at hand. That might include peaks that can indicate methyl carbons (~10-30 ppm). But we need count of methyl groups. Could also use proton NMR to see number of methyl signals (triplet etc). But we need to know integration.

Better: retrieve carbon shifts ranges for functional groups to identify methyl carbon peaks. But we need actual spectra.

Thus we need to call carbon_nmr_spectra to get data. Then count peaks in methyl region (around 10-30 ppm). However need to differentiate overlapping. Might be ambiguous.

Alternatively maybe the sample is known from context? No.

Thus we must request carbon_nmr_spectra.
